coding_standards: No hardcoded secrets or raw passwords in code or logs.
Shared state reads/writes on data_store must use data_lock.
Every handler change must be verified via scripts/validate_handlers.py.
All callback_data patterns must be defined in bot/handlers/callback_constants.py.
All type ignores must be documented in scripts/check_type_ignore.py and pass pyright.
Functions must maintain a threshold budget under 30 lines where possible.
All user-facing explanatory comments must prefer standard Arabic.
Synchronous blocking API calls inside async handlers must use run_blocking().
Exception handling must catch specific exceptions (TrapError, TelegramError, ConnectionError) before any catch-all with # noqa: BLE001.
Sensitive data (passwords, tokens, API keys) must be sanitized before logging or sending error responses.
Variables must have single unambiguous semantic meaning (no overloading version with error messages).
All external I/O calls must be enclosed in try/except with try/finally for cleanup when necessary.
User input must be validated (non-None, correct type) before forwarding to functions.
Critical context/state values must raise explicit errors instead of silent empty string defaults.
Function-level imports must have explicit rationale comments explaining circular import prevention.
